cases.event: One season, the power produced by a fictional rover working at {E} dropped sharply.
cases.q: What most likely caused the rover's power at {E} to drop?
restate: The rover's power at {E} dropped, and the question asks why.
Something caused the rover working at {E} to produce much less power.
cases.answer: Dust settling on the solar panels most likely caused the rover's power to drop, because the dust blocked sunlight from the panels.
cases.sum: the evidence points to dust on the solar panels as the reason the rover's power dropped.
cases.myth: The rover's power dropped because Mars moved farther from its moons.
cases.mythClause: the rover lost power only when it drove backward
cases.altText: Some engineers suggested that the rover's battery was failing.
cases.patternQ: What pattern connects the dust and the rover's power at {E}?
cases.patternA: The power dropped when dust settled on the panels and rose again after wind swept the panels clean, so the power followed the dust.
cases.patternSum: the rover's power fell when dust settled on the panels and rose when the panels were swept clean.

prediction.text: Early that season, an engineer predicted that the rover would lose the most power at night.
prediction.claim: the rover at {E} would lose the most power at night
prediction.whyNot: the power drop appeared during the day, while the panels were charging

cases.observerNote: The engineers checked the rover's power reports every day.

obs.text: The drop in power began during a dust storm at {E} that lasted {n0} days.
exps: the drop began during a dust storm, when dust would be settling on everything
the timing ties the lost power to the storm, not to the battery
a storm that long could leave a heavy coat of dust on the panels

obs.text: Pictures from the rover's arm camera showed a thick layer of dust on its solar panels.
exps: dust on the panels blocks sunlight, so the panels produce less power
this shows how the storm cut the power, since covered panels receive less light
a dusty layer explains the drop, because panels need light to make power

obs.text: When a gust of wind swept the panels clean, the power returned to about {n1} percent of normal within a day.
obs.tag: the power after the wind gust
exps: the power came back once the dust was gone, which is what would happen if dust were the cause
cleaning the panels fixed the problem, so the two are linked
once the cause was swept away, the effect faded

obs.text: A battery test showed that the rover's batteries could still hold a full charge.
exps: a battery that holds a full charge is not failing, so it cannot explain the drop
this rules out the battery, because it tested as healthy
with a healthy battery, the battery explanation has nothing to stand on

obs.text: The power drop at {E} appeared during the day, while the panels were charging, and not at night.
obs.tag: the timing of the power drop
exps: a failing battery would show up at night, when the rover depends on it, but the drop came during charging
this rules out the battery, since the problem appeared while the panels were working
a daytime drop points to the panels, not the battery
predExps: this directly contradicts the prediction, since the power drop happened during the day
if the rover lost the most power at night, the nighttime readings would show it, but they did not
the prediction expected a nighttime loss that never appeared
